title: Atomic Number — Meaning, Moseley's Evidence and Uses
topicTitle: Rutherford's atomic model and its limitations
notes: The atomic number Z: its definition, the X-ray evidence that made it the true identity of an element, and its uses. It belongs logically with Rutherford's model because Z is the nuclear charge his experiment revealed.

The atomic number Z is the number of protons in the nucleus — equivalently the nuclear charge in units of +e, or the number of electrons in the neutral atom. It is written as a left subscript (₁₁Na). In 1920 Rutherford named the nuclear charge 'atomic number'; it is now the defining property of an element.

Henry Moseley bombarded metal targets with fast cathode rays and measured the characteristic X-ray frequencies: $\sqrt{\nu}=a(Z-b)$. Plotting √ν against Z gives a straight line, but √ν against atomic mass does not — proving that Z, not atomic mass, is the fundamental quantity. This (i) corrected the anomalous pairs (Ar/K, Co/Ni, Te/I), (ii) gave isotopes one place in the table, (iii) fixed hydrogen's position, and (iv) predicted missing elements by gaps in the line.
• Identifies the element and fixes its position in the modern periodic table (periods by shell filling, groups by valence configuration).
• Gives the electron count of a neutral atom (e⁻ = Z) and the neutron count (n = A − Z).
• Enters Bohr-type formulas: rₙ ∝ n²/Z, Eₙ ∝ −Z²/n², ν of spectral lines ∝ Z² (used for He⁺, Li²⁺).
• In medicine/engineering Z governs X-ray absorption (bone vs tissue imaging) and shielding choices (lead, Z = 82).

Mass number A = Z + N (whole number); atomic mass is the weighted average over isotopes (e.g. Cl = 35.5 u from 75% ³⁵Cl + 25% ³⁷Cl). Only Z is unique to a chemical element — that is why the modern periodic law is stated in terms of Z.
confusion: ❌ Atomic number is the number of neutrons. ✅ It is the number of protons (nuclear charge); neutrons = A − Z.
❌ Elements are defined by atomic mass. ✅ Moseley showed the identity is Z; mass varies with isotopic composition.
❌ An ion has a different atomic number from its atom. ✅ Z never changes in chemistry — only the electron count does (Na and Na⁺ both Z = 11).

universalFacts: Moseley died at Gallipoli in 1915 at 27, shortly after establishing atomic number.
The 'missing' Z = 43 (technetium) and 61 (promethium) were later found — their X-ray lines had been predicted by gaps.
Beryllium's low Z = 4 makes it the window material of X-ray tubes (low absorption).
examples: **Problem:** An element has A = 23 and 12 neutrons. Identify it. **Solution:** Z = 23 − 12 = 11 → sodium (Na); in the neutral atom it has 11 electrons.

summary: The atomic number Z is the number of protons in the nucleus — equivalently the nuclear charge in units of +e, and the number of electrons in a neutral atom — and it is written as a left subscript, as in ₁₁Na. Rutherford named the nuclear charge 'atomic number' in 1920, and it is now the defining property of an element. Moseley's 1913 X-ray evidence settled the matter: bombarding metal targets with fast cathode rays and measuring the characteristic X-ray frequencies gives √ν = a(Z − b), so plotting √ν against Z gives a straight line while plotting it against atomic mass does not. Z therefore, not mass, is fundamental — which corrected the anomalous pairs (Ar/K, Co/Ni, Te/I), gave isotopes one place in the table, fixed hydrogen's position and predicted the missing elements Z = 43 and 61. Z fixes the table position, the electron and neutron counts (n = A − Z) and enters Bohr's formulas through r ∝ 1/Z, E ∝ −Z² and ν ∝ Z².
importantConcepts: Definition: Z = protons = nuclear charge in units of +e = electrons in a neutral atom, written as a left subscript
Moseley's law √ν = a(Z − b) from characteristic X-ray frequencies, 1913
Linear plot of √ν against Z but not against atomic mass, proving Z is the fundamental quantity
Consequences: corrected Ar/K, Co/Ni and Te/I; gave isotopes one place; fixed hydrogen's position
Uses: position in the periodic table, neutron count n = A − Z, Bohr-type dependences r ∝ 1/Z and E ∝ −Z², X-ray absorption and shielding
importantStatements: Z is the number of protons, never the number of neutrons; neutrons = A − Z.
Only Z is unique to a chemical element, which is why the modern periodic law is stated in terms of Z.
Z never changes in chemistry: Na and Na⁺ both have Z = 11, only the electron count differs.
Atomic mass is a weighted average over isotopes (Cl ≈ 35.45 u), so it is not a whole number and is not the identity of the element.
Moseley died at Gallipoli in 1915 at the age of 27, shortly after establishing atomic number.

keyPoints: Moseley's law involves the square root of frequency, not the frequency itself.
Z = p = e⁻ (neutral atom) and n = A − Z.
The missing elements Z = 43 (technetium) and 61 (promethium) were predicted from gaps in the line.
Beryllium's low Z = 4 makes it the window material of X-ray tubes because it absorbs X-rays least.
specialNotes: Link Z to the nuclear charge that Rutherford's scattering revealed — the two ideas belong together.
Lead's high Z = 82 is why it shields X-rays so effectively in medical and industrial use.
Isotopes share Z, so they occupy the same table position; that is exactly what Moseley's law made meaningful.
examShortTricks: Write √ν = a(Z − b) with the square root — a frequent one-mark item.
For any nuclide answer in one line: protons = Z, electrons = Z, neutrons = A − Z.
Quote one concrete Moseley correction (Ar/K, Co/Ni or Te/I) to earn the application mark.
